That's almost always about reference equality, not the values themselves.

React checks if props changed by comparing references, not by looking inside them. So even if two objects or arrays "look the same," a new one made on every render counts as different. The usual culprits are inline functions or objects passed as props, like `onClick={() => doThing()}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}` — those get rebuilt fresh every time the parent renders.

Two fixes work together:

1. Wrap the child in `React.memo()` so it skips re-rendering when props are equal.
2. Keep those function and object props stable with `useCallback` and `useMemo` in the parent, so they don't get rebuilt every time.

If the parent still re-renders often, `React.memo` alone won't help unless the props themselves are stable.
